units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Luxembourg. I'm Anna.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And I'm Ben.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I have to be honest with you, and with everyone listening.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: All I know about Luxembourg is that it's small and rich.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's more than most people know.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: How small, exactly?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You could drive across it in about an hour.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Its whole population is smaller than that of many a single city.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it's basically a very well-organized suburb.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Tell that to the emperors. For more than a thousand years, kings and emperors fought over this place.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's been a fortress, a province, a battlefield, a steel empire, a banking center, and a founding member of the European Union.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: All of that, in a country you can cross before lunch.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And it's the last grand duchy in the world.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait. Were there a lot of grand duchies?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Quite a few, once. Now there's one.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, I need to know how a place that small ended up that interesting.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Rock, iron, borders, and a great deal of stubbornness.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Right. New rule. I'm keeping an owner count.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Every time somebody new takes over Luxembourg, it goes on the board.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You're going to need a big board.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Starting at zero.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Not for long. And their national motto, by the way, translates as "we want to remain what we are."

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Which is a bold thing to say about a country that's changed hands more often than a second-hand bicycle.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Ha. Yes. Hold that thought.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So where do we start?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: With a swap of land beside a river.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: But first, a few thousand years we shouldn't skip.
